description: Japan single-source dependency for geostationary weather imagery: BoM services are critically dependent on JMA's Himawari, with Himawari-10 development delayed and the ALOS-4 SAR access channel unresolved.
treatment: Sustain the BoM-JMA Strategic Relationship Arrangement (11 November 2024) with Australian Himawari-10 co-investment; define custodian-confirmed contingency access to alternative imagery at comparable cadence (the input's stated success condition).

description: Interim military SATCOM rides on two single hosted payloads and one provider family: Optus C1 (aging, inclined orbit, contracted to September 2034 on 2022-vintage evidence) and Intelsat/SES IS-22 UHF (to at least 2033) - with SES describing limited comparable UHF capacity in the Indo-Pacific.
treatment: Deliver the SPA9102 sovereign UHF bird with availability-based support; design the wideband RFT for multi-provider award; hold IS-22 extension options (to 2041) as bridge, not destination.

description: Starlink has become the de facto Pacific disaster-resilience connectivity layer (Vanuatu earthquake response, Tonga restoration) - a single commercial provider under mixed regional governance, with the main alternative (Kacific) shrinking its satellite ambitions.
treatment: Promote the in-country community-gateway model (Nauru, Kosrae precedents), multi-vendor LEO procurement guidance through the CCRC research line, and cable redundancy (Tu'i Vava'u model) so no Pacific partner depends on one provider's policy.

description: Legacy single-orbit GEO concentration in military SATCOM persists until the multi-orbit architecture is delivered: the JP9102 cancellation rationale itself, with the first multi-orbit elements (sovereign LEO demonstrator) not due until early 2028.
treatment: Hold the NDS/IIP multi-orbit commitment through Second Pass; scope the alternative-space-communications line of effort; sequence the Optus/Inovor LEO demonstration (early 2028) as the proof point.

description: All Australian PNT rests on foreign-owned GNSS; SouthPAN - the flagship national augmentation - itself relies on GPS data as essential input, procures its space segment from a foreign operator, and excludes northern Australia from planned Safety-of-Life coverage.
treatment: Layered mitigation per the ADF multi-layered PNT approach: M-code access, sovereign quantum timing (TEMPO.Space), LEO-PNT evaluation, and the ANCHOR-recommended national PNT policy (none exists as of February 2026).

description: National SDA sensing is concentrated on one peninsula: the SST, C-band radar and DARC Site 1 all sit at or beside Harold E. Holt, Exmouth - a single geographic point of failure for weather, attack or accident.
treatment: Geographic dispersal through the commercial layer (LeoLabs south-west WA radar, EOS Mount Stromlo/Learmonth, Silentium Swan Reach SA) and reliance on DARC Sites 2-3 (UK 2030, third US site) for global redundancy.

description: Every opportunity in the portfolio draws on a nascent space workforce: first ADF Space Initial Employment Training graduates June 2026, the Joint PNT Directorate is ~17 people, and the DSR-directed workforce method is not evidenced as established.
treatment: Partner training pipelines as the fastest levers: JCO-200 course line, reciprocal Japan exchanges, US embeds and command billets, exercise repetitions (OPP-21); sequence new commitments against workforce reality rather than ambition.
